business_problem: Nextory is one of Europe’s largest sources for audiobooks, ebooks, and digital magazines. Working with hundreds of publishers across the world, the streaming platform aims to provide readers with everything from the latest releases to the classics.
solution_summary: Nextory worked with Google Cloud to map, analyze, and modernize its media processing system in just eight weeks using agentic AI. Nextory is one of Europe’s largest sources for audiobooks, ebooks, and digital magazines. Working with hundreds of publishers across the world, the streaming platform aims to provide readers with everything from the latest releases to the classics. Each new publishing agreement means back catalogs of hundreds of thousands of titles to process at once—something Nextory’s legacy Ruby on Rails architecture was increasingly struggling to keep up with. Nextory and saw a chance not only to rebuild our ingestion system, but also learn a repeatable way to use agentic AI on legacy code,” explains Mattias Engblom, CTO at Nextory.

solution_components.name: Antigravity
solution_components.role: Analyzes legacy code and helps engineers plan large refactors of core application workflows.

solution_components.name: Gemini CLI
solution_components.role: Extends Google Cloud-assisted development into command-line engineering workflows.

solution_components.name: Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE)
solution_components.role: Orchestrates the platform's containerized services and high-concurrency workloads.

solution_components.name: Cloud Run
solution_components.role: Runs serverless application services and APIs with automatic scaling for bursty workloads.

solution_components.name: Pub/Sub
solution_components.role: Moves high-volume events and API traffic between services so the workflow stays decoupled and resilient.
